# Remove-ZbxDiscoveryRule

## SYNOPSIS

Removes discovery rules.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxDiscoveryRule [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixDiscoveryRule>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A low-level discovery rule finds the parts of a host that come and go, such as file systems, network interfaces or databases, and creates items, triggers and graphs for each from prototypes. The Remove-ZbxDiscoveryRule cmdlet deletes the discovery rules given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with discoveryrule.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a discovery rule

```powershell
Get-ZbxDiscoveryRule -Host 'web-01' -Name 'Mounted filesystems' | Remove-ZbxDiscoveryRule -Confirm:$false
```

Deletes the discovery rule Mounted filesystems of web-01. -Confirm:$false skips the prompt the command shows by default.

### Example 2: Preview deleting a discovery rule

```powershell
Get-ZbxDiscoveryRule -Host 'web-01' -Name 'Mounted filesystems' | Remove-ZbxDiscoveryRule -WhatIf
```

-WhatIf shows what the command would delete, and deletes nothing.
